title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 80-83): Grothendieck studies the Galois action of Γ = Gal(K̄/K) on the profinite fundamental groupoid Π̂_1(X_K̄) of an algebraic variety X over a number field K. A rational point x ∈ X(K), together with a base point x0, gives a path torsor and hence a class in H^1(Γ, Π̂_1). He also has cocycles f_ℓ(u), g_ℓ(u) attached to paths ℓ and to u ∈ Γ. On the previous page he hopes for explicit formulas computing these classes from the arithmetic of the point x. He notes that the Mordell–Weil/Néron argument for injectivity of 'points → classes' already works after abelianisation. This reduces the question to an abelian variety, or more generally to a semi-abelian variety: a generalized Jacobian (Albanese) of X, which is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus.

This page states the limitation of that reduction. For such commutative group varieties the Γ-action on the profinite groupoid is far from faithful. Examples: an elliptic curve, where the action is through the Tate module and kills Gal(K̄/K(E[∞])); or G_m, where the action is through the cyclotomic character and kills Gal(K̄/K(μ_∞)). So invariants of the type f_ℓ(u) attached to X alone cannot 'locate' (repérer) an element u ∈ Γ. One must bring in 'location parameters' for u coming from other K-varieties, the most natural being U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Implicitly, its Galois action is faithful (Belyi), and u can be coordinatised by its action on π̂_1(U_{0,3}).

The page then starts a new paragraph on functoriality. For a morphism of K-schemes f: X → Y, the induced morphisms of groupoids Π_1(X) → Π_1(Y) and Π̂_1(X) → Π̂_1(Y) commute with the Γ-action, by the schematic description of Π̂_1. On the next page this gives compatibility of the cocycles: f̂(f_ℓ(u)) = f_{f̂(ℓ)}(u), and likewise for g. The overall programme combines several pieces: Kummer/section-type classes of points (a precursor of the section conjecture); the abelian (Jacobian) part handled by Mordell–Weil; and Galois elements parametrised through their action on π̂_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}). This last piece prefigures the Ihara/Drinfeld (χ(u), f_u) parametrisation and GT.
errors: The groupoid on which Γ acts must be the profinite Π̂_1(X_K̄), not the discrete Π_1(X_K) as written. This is a notational slip, since Γ does not act on the discrete topological groupoid.
'Generalized Jacobian' is meant as a semi-abelian variety (extension of an abelian variety by a torus). The parenthetical 'par un tore' is loose but harmless.
Not an error but a gap: the faithfulness of Γ on π̂_1(U_{0,3}) is used implicitly, not proved. It follows from Belyi (1979).

ideas.what: Non-faithfulness of the Galois action on the profinite fundamental groupoid of commutative group varieties (elliptic curves, G_m), contrasted implicitly with anabelian varieties.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness of outer Galois representations for hyperbolic curves vs. abelian/toric case
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi 1979 (P^1−3 points); Matsumoto 1996 (affine hyperbolic curves); Hoshi–Mochizuki 2011 (proper hyperbolic curves)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), where faithfulness of Γ_Q on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) via Belyi is discussed; letter to Faltings (1983) on anabelian varieties

ideas.what: Using U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞} as the universal auxiliary variety providing 'location parameters' for elements u of the Galois group.
ideas.modern_name: Ihara/Drinfeld parametrisation u ↦ (χ(u), f_u) ∈ Ẑ* × F̂_2'; embedding Γ_Q ↪ GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1980s), Drinfeld (1990), building on Belyi; Grothendieck's Esquisse

ideas.what: Reduction of the point-to-class map to the abelianised fundamental group via generalized Jacobian/Albanese and Mordell–Weil.
ideas.modern_name: Kummer map for (semi-)abelian varieties; abelian/injectivity part of the section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory; Grothendieck letter to Faltings 1983
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), in Geometric Galois Actions vol. 1

ideas.what: Functoriality: a morphism f: X→Y gives Γ-equivariant morphisms of profinite fundamental groupoids, and the associated cocycles are compatible.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of étale fundamental groupoids / Galois equivariance (SGA1)

missed.claim: If the archive dating ('à partir de 1978') applies to this page, Grothendieck already singles out U_{0,3} as the canonical variety for 'locating' Galois elements, independently of or just before Belyi's 1979 theorem. Esquisse instead presents Belyi's theorem as the trigger. The page explicitly frames this as the remedy for the non-faithfulness of the abelian (Jacobian/torus) part of the theory.
missed.quote: Il faudra donc de façon essentielle introduire des "paramètres de repérage" pour u, en utilisant d'autres variétés algébriques déf sur K - la plus naturelle étant (35) U_{0,3} = P^1 \ {0,1,∞}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it clarifies the genesis of the GT/Ihara-parameter viewpoint and its link to the explicit-formula programme for path-torsor classes of rational points (section-conjecture side). The dating is uncertain, though.

missed.claim: The programme of explicit arithmetic formulas for the classes f_ℓ(u) of paths to rational points, with Galois elements coordinatised via their action on π̂_1(U_{0,3}), is announced but not carried out. The idea is to combine Kummer/Mordell–Weil data with the Ihara-type parameters of u.
missed.quote: il ne suffit pas de connaître des invariants du type f_ℓ(u) relatifs à ce X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Partial analogues exist: Anderson–Ihara, Nakamura's explicit formulas for Galois action on paths (ℓ-adic polylogarithmic characters), and Wojtkowiak. A systematic version for paths to arbitrary rational points on curves remains only partially developed.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly known ideas that are articulated in Esquisse and the Faltings letter. The mild interest is the early explicit diagnosis: abelian quotients are not faithful, so U_{0,3} is needed as a universal 'repérage' device. If the dating is right, this possibly predates the publicly stated Belyi-triggered motivation.

'invariants du type J_ℓ^{ass}' is probably 'invariants du type f_ℓ(u)' or similar cocycle notation; the struck word before it is likely 'des'.
'la variété G_m(C) = C*': the handwriting looks like 'G_m(C)' (or T_m), which is consistent.
In (36) the target is written as a crossed-out X corrected to Y: f : X → Y.
The underlined phrase is 'relatifs à ce [même] X' with 'même' struck out.
